overview: The Medford City Council met to honor community members, approve public safety and environmental initiatives, and pass several municipal ordinances. Notable actions included ordaining a revised Human Rights Commission ordinance and updating rules on property overgrowth and rodent control.

items.title: Commendation of Ladder 2 Crew
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending the crew of Ladder 2 for their heroic actions rescuing two individuals during a structure fire.

items.title: West Medford Community Center 90th Anniversary
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating the 90th anniversary of the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Commendation of Vice President Kit Collins
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Vice President Collins for her outstanding municipal service from 2022 to 2026.

items.title: Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the December 2, 2025, meeting alongside committee reports from the Committee of the Whole, Resident Services, and Public Health.

items.title: Medford Standard Compensation Ordinance
items.summary: Referred the proposed Medford Standard Compensation Ordinance to a Committee of the Whole and requested a legal opinion from KP Law.

items.title: Acceptance of M.G.L. Chapter 40, Section 71 (School Bus Stop Arm Cameras)
items.summary: Approved the local adoption of state law enabling the installation and maintenance of automated violation detection monitoring systems on school buses.

items.title: Human Rights Commission Ordinance Revision
items.summary: Ordained the amended Human Rights Commission Ordinance on third reading, incorporating a reference to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

items.title: McGlynn School Solar Panels PPA Lease Agreement
items.summary: Approved a 20-year power purchase agreement with Solect Energy to install and maintain solar panels at the McGlynn School.

items.title: 9-1-1 Dispatchers Union Wage Adjustment
items.summary: Approved a multi-year wage adjustment agreement for the 9-1-1 Dispatchers Union.

items.title: CPA Appropriation for Riverside Plaza Shade Improvements Project
items.summary: Approved a $40,000 Community Preservation Act appropriation from the Open Space Reserve for contingency needs on the Riverside Plaza Shade Improvements Project.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriation for Innes Associates
items.summary: Approved an $85,330 appropriation from the Capital Stabilization Fund for a contract extension with Innes Associates for zoning consultant services.

items.title: MOU with Mystic Valley Development Commission
items.summary: Authorized a Memorandum of Understanding with the Mystic Valley Development Commission for mitigation payments to Malden regarding the Rivers Edge project.

items.title: DPW Personnel Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Ordained personnel ordinance amendments restructuring classifications and salaries for the Assistant City Engineer and Project Manager positions.

items.title: Resolution to Withdraw Residential Rezoning Proposal
items.summary: Approved a resolution to withdraw the current residential rezoning proposal from the Community Development Board and refer it back to the Planning and Permitting Committee.

items.title: Resolution to Sever Medford Square and West Medford Square Zoning Proposals
items.summary: Approved a resolution to sever the joint Medford Square and West Medford Square zoning proposals, referring the former to the Community Development Board and the latter to the Planning and Permitting Committee.

items.title: Overgrowth Ordinance
items.summary: Ordained an amendment creating an overgrowth ordinance to allow the Board of Health to address public health hazards on private properties.

items.title: Rodent Control Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Ordained amendments to the rodent control ordinance to expand the Board of Health's enforcement and remediation authority on private properties.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Heard public comments concerning federal immigration enforcement, local rodenticide use, and safety improvements at the Route 60 rotary.
